argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a narrowed form: launch readiness is supported for the tested configuration because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.0 percentage points, has no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passes general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same record also shows that protocol eligibility support is a named deployment context whose evaluations are not yet in the packet. That means the defensible position is not clean certification with no limitation; it is certification conditioned on explicit disclosure that protocol eligibility support remains an unresolved evaluation gap and should be treated as unknown pending queued tests. On that narrowed claim, the packet is supportable and does not require escalation beyond a caveated compliance treatment.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support the policy analysis. The practical effect of treating this as caveated rather than suspicious is that it preserves the supported readiness finding for the tested configuration while aligning the certification record to the disclosed evaluation gap, instead of forcing unnecessary escalation over an overbroad wording problem.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not permit a clean or unqualified certification claim here. It does permit certification support for the tested configuration when general readiness evidence is present, provided material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts are disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. No approved risk acceptance is in evidence, so disclosure is the available compliance path on this record.
concessions: A clean certification with no deployment limitation is not supported by the admissible record.
The packet does not establish completed evaluation coverage for protocol eligibility support.
The draft model-card position that missing evaluations imply no known limitations is too broad on this evidence.
Absent approved risk acceptance, the unresolved named-context gap must be disclosed.
